svg.text: STACK OVERFLOW — THE VOTE PATH (IDEMPOTENCY)
castVote — one algorithm, two callers
① ENTRY — voteQuestion(qId, voterId, UPVOTE)
voteAnswer(aId, ...) is the SAME call with a different VoteTarget
VoteTarget { void apply(int delta); } — a one-method callback, Command-ish
② GUARDS — before any state moves
voter exists · target exists · voterId != authorId
self-vote ⇒ SelfVoteException (a checked domain error, not a silent no-op)
③ BUILD THE LEDGER KEY
voteKey = voterId + ":" + (Q|A) + ":" + targetId
the rule "one voter, one post" lives IN THE KEY — no scan needed ✓
④ THE CRITICAL SECTION — votes.compute(voteKey, ...)
CHM.compute is an atomic read-modify-write PER KEY. No lock object to invent.
int[] reputationDelta = new int[1];
votes.compute(voteKey, (key, existing) -> {
if (existing == voteType) throw new DuplicateVoteException();
if (existing != null) { // changing the vote
target.apply(-existing.getValue()); // UNDO the old one
reputationDelta[0] -= policy.reputationForVote(existing); }
target.apply(voteType.getValue()); ... return voteType; });
re-casting the same vote is an ERROR, not a silent no-op — the caller should know ✓
changing a vote undoes the old delta AND the old reputation, in one atomic step
⑤ APPLY REPUTATION — OUTSIDE the bin lock
applyReputation(authorId, reputationDelta[0]) → fires ReputationListeners
a slow listener can't stall every other vote hashing to the same bin ✓
TWO SEPARATE MISTAKES
THE ORIGINAL CODE
synchronized (voteKey.intern()) { ... }
(a) NEVER lock on an interned string
intern() returns a JVM-wide canonical instance. Unrelated code
anywhere in the process that locks a string with the same content
shares your monitor — invisible contention, an unfindable deadlock,
and user-derived keys pile up in the string pool.
(b) THE LOCK SCOPE WAS WRONG — the interesting one
The lock was per (voter, target). The COUNTERS are per target.
Two different voters take two different locks ⇒ they serialize
against nobody, and voteCount += v loses updates.
THE FIX — two concerns, two mechanisms
Idempotency (scope = the vote key) → CHM.compute
already atomic per key; nothing to allocate, nothing to leak
Counters (scope = the POST) → AtomicInteger
voteCount, viewCount, reputation — getting the lock right without
this changes nothing at all
Reputation floor → a CAS loop, not add-then-clamp
reputation.accumulateAndGet(points, (c,d) -> Math.max(0, c + d));
MEASURED — 200 distinct voters upvote one question
before: voteCount = 194 / 195 / 178 / 179 of 200
after : 200 / 200 on every trial, authorRep = 2001 ✓
Reputation was corrupted WORSE than the score — same race, on reputation += points.
THE FOUR OUTCOMES OF A VOTE
existing = votes.get(voterId:TYPE:targetId)
existing == null → FIRST VOTE
score += ±1 · author reputation += (+10 upvote / −2 downvote)
the deltas come from VoteType and ReputationPolicy, never from a literal
existing == voteType → DUPLICATE
throw DuplicateVoteException — no state moves at all
a deliberate product choice: the caller learns, rather than silently succeeding
existing != voteType → CHANGED VOTE
undo the old delta, then apply the new one — a net swing of 2
reputation is reversed and re-applied the same way
both halves inside one compute() — never a half-applied vote ✓
voter == author → SelfVoteException, before the ledger is touched
reputation never drops below zero, so a downvote storm floors at 0 rather than going negative
ACCEPT — the OTHER compound mutation
Accepting a SECOND answer must un-accept the first AND claw back its +15 —
otherwise reputation inflates every time the author changes their mind.
synchronized (q) { // the QUESTION is the monitor
q.getAcceptedAnswerId().ifPresent(prevId -> {
prev.unmarkAsAccepted();
applyReputation(prev.getAuthorId(), -policy.reputationForAcceptedAnswer());
q.acceptAnswer(a.getId()); a.markAsAccepted(); applyReputation(+15); }
the monitor is the QUESTION because the invariant is scoped to it ✓
different questions never contend · author-only, no privilege escape hatch (unlike close)
SAY IT OUT LOUD:
"Idempotency and counter arithmetic are two different scopes. compute() gives me the first, atomics give me the second. Locking one and forgetting the other still loses votes."
THE SAME SHAPE, THREE TIMES — let the map arbitrate
registerUser: usernameIndex.putIfAbsent(key, id) — 32 threads on "dupe" gave 2–4 successes before the fix.
Order matters: claim the name, THEN publish the user. Reversed, a lost claim leaves an orphan user reachable by id.
castVote: votes.compute(...) · acceptAnswer: synchronized (question) — pick the monitor that matches the invariant's scope.
HONEST GAPS IN THIS IMPLEMENTATION
getQuestion() increments viewCount — a getter with a side effect, and a single-counter hotspot on popular posts.
Score and reputation are denormalized: two sources of truth that can drift. Reconcile by replaying the votes ledger.
Search is an O(questions) scan · no rate limiting, so nothing here stops a voting ring · no JUnit harness for these races yet.
LEGEND

g.text: Invariants defended: N distinct voters ⇒ score exactly N · one vote per (voter, post) · at most one accepted answer
In a real DB all of this becomes a UNIQUE(voter_id, target_type, target_id) plus UPDATE ... SET score = score + ?
